slides.title: Complex Manifolds: The Chapter Map
slides.notes: Open by telling students that Chapter 9 changes the unit of measurement: the real tangent space is still present, but every construction is now asked to respect multiplication by i. The lecture will keep three questions synchronized: which data defines the complex direction, which hypotheses make it integrable, and which metrics or connections preserve it.

slides.title: From Real Tangent Spaces To Complex Directions
slides.notes: Stress that a complex structure on a real vector space is not extra notation for coordinates. It is an operator J with square minus the identity, so every admissible basis arrives in pairs. The diagram should make the pairing visible before any complex coordinate symbols are introduced.

slides.title: Type Decomposition: (1,0) And (0,1)
slides.notes: Use the split into type (1,0) and type (0,1) directions as the first major payoff of the algebra. The audience should see that complexification doubles the room, while the eigenvalue test separates holomorphic and antiholomorphic motion into complementary lanes.

slides.title: Almost Complex Structures: Algebra Becomes Field
slides.notes: Move from algebra at one tangent space to a smooth field of operators on the whole manifold. Almost complex means the pointwise algebra is available everywhere; it does not yet guarantee holomorphic charts. That distinction is the hinge for the next integrability slide.

slides.title: Integrability: When J Comes From Holomorphic Charts
slides.notes: Present integrability as the difference between a formal rotation rule and coordinates that genuinely behave holomorphically. The Nijenhuis torsion is the obstruction detector. When it vanishes, brackets of type (1,0) fields stay in the expected type and the local complex language becomes honest.

slides.title: Forms Split Into Bidegrees
slides.notes: Forms inherit the same type bookkeeping as tangent vectors, and this is where the chapter begins to feel computational. Explain that d can be inspected by its type-changing pieces. On a complex manifold, the clean partial and conjugate-partial split becomes a practical diagnostic.

slides.title: Connections That Preserve J
slides.notes: A connection in this chapter is useful only if it knows about J. The slide should connect the bundle of complex linear frames with the equation parallel J equals zero. Once a connection preserves J, torsion and curvature are forced to satisfy complex-linear identities.

slides.title: Hermitian Metrics And The Fundamental Form
slides.notes: Emphasize that a Hermitian metric is a Riemannian metric that treats J as an isometry. The fundamental two-form packages the same data in skew form. This pairing is the bridge from metric geometry to the exterior-form tests that define the Kaehler condition.

slides.title: Kaehler Condition: Three Equivalent Lenses
slides.notes: This is the central compression slide for Kaehler geometry. The audience should leave with three interchangeable lenses: the Levi-Civita connection preserves J, the fundamental form is closed, and the complex structure is integrable with the compatible metric. Each lens supports a different computation.

slides.title: Local Coordinates: Reading The Metric Matrix
slides.notes: Local coordinates are not merely notation here; they are the practical place where a Kaehler metric becomes a Hermitian matrix of functions. Point out how symmetry and derivative identities reduce the number of independent coefficients and make curvature formulas readable.

slides.title: Curvature In Complex Notation
slides.notes: Curvature in complex notation has fewer live components than an arbitrary Riemannian curvature tensor. Use the block diagram to show why Kaehler symmetries remove many mixed terms. The Ricci form is then a trace of the curvature, not a mysterious new object.

slides.title: The Example Zoo: Flat, Projective, Ball
slides.notes: Keep the examples as models, not as a catalogue to memorize. Flat complex space, projective space with positive curvature, the ball with negative curvature, tori, and Grassmannians show how the same Kaehler grammar appears in different global settings.

slides.title: Holomorphic Sectional Curvature
slides.notes: Holomorphic sectional curvature is the sectional curvature of a J-invariant two-plane. It is more selective than ordinary sectional curvature, but in the Kaehler setting it carries enough information to organize the full curvature tensor under the chapter's symmetry assumptions.

slides.title: Complex Space Forms
slides.notes: Use the sign diagram as a classification preview. Positive constant holomorphic curvature points toward complex projective space, zero toward complex Euclidean space, and negative toward the complex ball. The point is not proof by picture; it is orientation for the subsequent rigidity theorem.

slides.title: De Rham Splitting In The Kaehler World
slides.notes: De Rham decomposition gains extra structure in the Kaehler category because parallel transport respects J. Riemannian factors can be paired with complex factors, and non-degeneracy becomes a statement about which parallel pieces remain. This links holonomy, product geometry, and complex coordinates.

slides.title: Submanifolds Inherit The Curvature Test
slides.notes: For complex submanifolds, the normal space is also J-invariant, so the second fundamental form satisfies complex compatibility identities. The Gauss equation then explains why ambient holomorphic sectional curvature controls the submanifold's corresponding curvature, with a visible correction term.

slides.title: Hermitian Vector Bundles And The Chern Connection
slides.notes: Close the theory arc with Hermitian vector bundles. The Chern connection is the unique connection compatible with the Hermitian metric and holomorphic structure. Its curvature supplies the local form formulas behind Ricci-type quantities and later characteristic-class constructions.

slides.title: Notebook Lab And Instructor Checklist
slides.notes: Tie the deck back to the notebook lab. The notebook's dependency graph, local chart model, and invariant table are deliberately small, but they train the same reading habit: turn definitions into checkable data, watch which hypotheses preserve type, and make curvature or metric claims answer a concrete inspection question.
